ai.title: Refactor knowledge system prompt structure and guidelines
ai.summary: Moved Knowledge section to end of system prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts. Expanded content types to include project mission and user intent, while adding explicit exclusions for verbose or redundant documentation. Updated guidelines to enforce conciseness, command verbs, and markdown usage for better agent performance.

eli5.text: The way your coding assistant is being prompted to understand and remember project details has been reorganized. The section that tells the assistant how to keep track of important project notes was moved to the end of its instructions, and the guidance on what kinds of notes to record, how to write them, and how to format them was rewritten to be shorter and clearer. If you looked at the assistant's setup, you would see that its instructions now emphasize keeping notes brief and focused on big-picture project goals rather than documenting every small detail, and it now explicitly tells the assistant to avoid writing long, redundant explanations of code. This change is live today and affects how the assistant builds and maintains its internal knowledge base for your projects, making it

ai.title: Add file-based debug logging and fix duplicate file processing
ai.summary: New `backend/src/debug.ts` introduces `debugLog` and `clearDebugLog` for file-based logging to `debug.log`, gated by `DEBUG_MODE`. `backend/src/prompts.ts` uses a `processedFiles` Set to prevent duplicate `processFileBlock` calls for the same path. `backend/src/server.ts` clears the log on startup. `.gitignore` excludes `debug.log`. `musings.knowledge.md` documents edit/diff block issues.

eli5.text: Today, if you ask the assistant to edit a file, it will no longer accidentally process the same file twice in one request, which could have caused conflicting or duplicated changes. While working, you (or anyone watching the backend logs) might also notice a new plain-text file named debug.log being written in the backend folder, capturing a step-by-step trace of each assistant task for troubleshooting; this file is not tracked by the project's file history tool and is wiped clean each time the server restarts. The debug log is always on for now, so no setting must be toggled to see it.

ai.title: ESC key stops generation in CLI
ai.summary: Escape key interrupts active response generation in CLI. Sets raw mode stdin listener; checks `stopResponseRequested` flag in `sendUserInputAndAwaitResponse`. Prevents assistant message persistence on abort. Limited to `src/index.ts`.

eli5.text: You can now press the Escape key to stop the assistant from generating a response while you're chatting, and when you do, it will stop mid-sentence and won't save that partial reply to your conversation history. This works by listening for your keystroke in real-time and telling the response generator to quit, so the only sign you'll notice is a brief 'Response stopped by user' message and the assistant going quiet instead of finishing its answer.

ai.title: System prompt restructured with explicit recommendations
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts restructures the project files section, replacing a dense paragraph with a bulleted Recommendations list. Adds guidance to batch-read multiple files in a single read_files call for request understanding. Scope limited to backend system prompt. The read-before-edit constraint remains, now isolated as a distinct bullet.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal instructions for handling coding projects were rewritten to be clearer. Instead of a dense paragraph about reading files, the guidance is now broken into short bullet points. One point tells the assistant to read multiple files at once when trying to understand a request, rather than checking files one by one. Another point reminds the assistant it must read a file before editing it. Nothing changes for you as a user, but the assistant may work more smoothly and efficiently on coding tasks.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to edit a file for you, it now writes out the full change directly instead of showing you instructions like 'Add this line here.' You will see the completed edit applied automatically, without needing to copy anything yourself. This only affects how edits look in your session today.

ai.title: Revert debug log expansion and file deduplication in prompts.ts
ai.summary: Reverts experimental debug logging expansion in backend/src/prompts.ts, restoring standard indentation and removing verbose message length tracking. Disables automatic clearing of debug logs in backend/src/server.ts to preserve initial issue context. Removes processedFiles deduplication logic and uniqueChanges mapping, restoring direct file processing and raw change return.

eli5.text: The assistant temporarily turned down some experimental logging features so the team can investigate the root cause of early problems. This means verbose tracking of message lengths and file deduplication was paused, and the system now returns raw file changes instead of deduplicated ones. If you looked at the debug output right now, you would see less detail and possibly some duplicate file entries. This rollback is live today across the backend and file processing components.

ai.title: Refine indentation analysis in backend prompt
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/prompts.ts` to require explicit analysis of indentation style (spaces/tabs), level size, and nesting depth instead of assuming fixed spacing. Instructions now emphasize exact character-for-character matching for `<old>` blocks, including empty lines, and mandate maintaining original indentation in `<new>` blocks. This internal refinement targets the backend prompt logic to improve string replacement accuracy.

eli5.text: When the assistant makes code changes, it must now carefully analyze the original file's indentation first - checking whether it uses spaces or tabs, how many spaces per level, and how deeply nested the code is. The instructions also now require it to match every single character exactly when replacing code, including empty lines, rather than just the non-blank parts. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment to the internal prompt logic and is already in place.

ai.title: Save partial assistant responses on stop
ai.summary: src/index.ts persists assistant messages regardless of stopResponseRequested flag. Previously, stopping generation discarded the partial response. Now logs '[Response stopped by user. Partial response saved.]' after saving. Also refactors ESC key handling to constant and applies prettier formatting to chatStorage calls.

eli5.text: Now when you hit the stop button to cancel the assistant's response mid-message, any text it had already written gets saved to the conversation instead of being thrown away. You might see a small log note like '[Response stopped by user. Partial response saved.]' in the system output. This only affects the internal chat tool and doesn't change anything you can see on the surface.

ai.title: Remove applyReplacement helper
ai.summary: Deleted applyReplacement from backend/src/prompts.ts. processFileBlock now uses direct String.includes and replace with trimmed content. Removed flexible whitespace and indentation matching logic.

eli5.text: When the system tries to swap in a new version of part of your file, it used to try hard to guess where to put it even if the text didn't line up exactly. Now that it doesn't find an exact copy of the old text, it simply skips the change instead of guessing. You might see more skipped edits in your debug logs, and behind the scenes the helper that did the guessing was removed. This is live today and only affects how file edits are applied behind the scenes, no new behavior for you.

ai.title: Add message history to diff prompt context
ai.summary: Message history injected into diff generation prompt via `processFileBlock` and `generateDiffBlocks` in `backend/src/prompts.ts`. Provides conversational context to Claude for more accurate code changes. Scope: backend prompt engineering. Detail: `Message[]` passed through call chain, formatted as `<message_history>` block before old/new content.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to update your code, it can now see the conversation you've already had right alongside the code it's changing, so its edits line up better with what you asked for. The assistant already shows these improved edits today whenever you're modifying an existing file through the chat. You'd notice fewer edits that miss the mark or need correcting because the assistant is no longer guessing what you meant.

ai.title: Enforce file path in diff generation and system prompt
ai.summary: generateDiffBlocks now requires filePath to tag logs and enforce path in file blocks via createFileBlock. System prompt upgrades read_files recommendations to strict important_instructions to prevent stale edits. Covers backend prompts.ts and system-prompt.ts. Diff blocks now explicitly include paths, replacing createFileBlockWithoutPath usage in examples.

eli5.text: The assistant now keeps track of which file it is working on when it generates edits, so it no longer mixes up changes meant for different files. This affects the behind-the-scenes instructions that guide how the assistant reads and edits project files, making file paths appear explicitly when changes are created and logged. If you looked at a session of the assistant editing files today, you'd notice that every edit block now clearly shows which file path it belongs to instead of sometimes leaving that blank.

ai.title: Server-initiated file read via WebSocket actions
ai.summary: Added `read-files` and `read-files-response` actions to WebSocket schema. Server requests file contents from client, replacing static `fileContext`. `getFiles` now returns `null` for missing paths instead of throwing. `filterObject` added to `common/src/util/object.ts` to strip nulls in `getKnowledgeFiles`.

eli5.text: The assistant can now ask your computer to immediately read the latest version of a file before it writes any changes to that file, instead of guessing from an earlier snapshot. If the file you name doesn't actually exist, the assistant will get a clear "not found" signal rather than stopping the whole session. If you peek at the settings, you'll spot a couple of new message types that let the assistant and your project swap these file reads back and forth. This rolls out live today to anyone using the assistant over a WebSocket connection, meaning the moment you ask it to edit a file, it pulls the current contents first.

ai.title: Add file reading and knowledge update instructions to prompt
ai.summary: Appends `<additional_instruction>` tags to the last user message in `promptClaudeAndGetFileChanges` (`backend/src/prompts.ts`). Directs the agent to request files via `read_files` and update knowledge files when learning from feedback. Removes debug logging in `requestFiles` (`backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`).

eli5.text: The coding helper was given new reminders so it asks for more of your project files when trying to understand your question, and it can save what it learns into a reference notebook for next time. You would notice the assistant requesting extra files during a session and occasionally updating stored notes after figuring something out. The team also turned off a temporary debug message that was cluttering the file-reading connection logs. This is live now in the backend that powers the assistant's file handling.

ai.title: Fix prompt diff trimming bug
ai.summary: backend/src/prompts.ts now trims oldContent and newContent during blockRegex parsing instead of during processFileBlock replacement. This prevents exact-match failures when diff blocks contain leading or trailing whitespace. src/project-files.ts updates the failure console.log message for clarity. musings.knowledge.md adds a documentation scraping use case.

eli5.text: You might have noticed the assistant occasionally failed to apply a requested edit, even when the old and new text looked like a perfect match. The mismatch was caused by invisible spaces or blank lines at the edges of the text the assistant was trying to swap, which tripped up the lookup. Those edge spaces are now stripped at the moment a block of text is pulled from your instructions, so edits that look identical will be applied instead of being skipped. The behind-the-scenes console messages that show up when editing fails were also reworded to be clearer.
